name: gov_sso_webview_rules
source: omnisec/mega-analyzer gov-SSO & WebView auth-flow taxonomy (validated on ru.dnevnik.app ESIA login)

rules.title: WebView SSL error bypass: SslErrorHandler.proceed() accepts an invalid certificate. In SSO/gov-auth flows this exposes the login page (and any ticket/token scraped from it) to MITM. Works across smali and Java sources; fires at the call site, so event-driven Kotlin that splits onReceivedSslError from the proceed() lambda is still caught.
Government SSO endpoint (Gosuslugi/ESIA) referenced from code: gov identity provider is part of the auth flow. Inventory finding — map which classes build or intercept these URLs.

Hardcoded OAuth client credentials: two UUID literals within a short window in a file that also mentions token/authorization endpoints. Extractable client_id/client_secret pairs (as found shipping in refresh-token interceptors) let anyone impersonate the app against the auth API.

WebView page HTML is dumped via evaluateJavascript + innerHTML. When the page is an SSO/login form this scrapes auth state (tickets, task ids) out of the DOM instead of using a documented redirect/callback — spoofable by anything that can alter the page.

WebViewClient handles intent:// URLs by parsing them into an Intent and starting an activity. A page (or MITM peer, if SSL errors are also bypassed) can launch arbitrary components/deep links inside the app.
